t: The Mongol realm that Genghis Khan allotted to his son Chagatai, spanning Central Asia's steppe and Silk Road cities.
It produced Timur and, through him, a Chagataid line that helped legitimise the Mughal emperors of India.
Torn between nomadic tribes and settled Muslim cities, it split apart, losing Transoxiana to Timur by 1370.
dyk: The city of Qarshi in Uzbekistan takes its name from the palace that Kebek Khan built there, near Nasaf, in the early 14th century.
ev: Chagatai Khan begins his rule over the appanage allotted by Genghis Khan
Alghu exploits the Mongol civil war to assert real independence
Qutlugh Khwaja leads a great Chagataid army to the outskirts of Delhi
Kebek Khan introduces a standardised silver coinage, the kebeks
Eastern nomadic tribes revolt against Tarmashirin and overthrow him
Tughlugh Timur briefly reunites the khanate
Timur completes his seizure of power in Transoxiana
The Yarkent Khanate is founded as a Chagataid successor state
